coachingPoints: Establish the pivot foot the instant you catch or stop — hesitation causes travels.
Keep the ball tight to your body while pivoting; loose balls get stripped.
Front pivot (toward the defender) for quick drives; reverse pivot (away) for protection.
Stay low and balanced — pivots from a tall stance are slow and wobbly.
Pivot with purpose: every pivot should create an angle for a pass, shot, or drive.
commonMistakes: Lifting the pivot foot before passing or shooting — the most-called travel in basketball.
Pivoting with the ball held low and away — defenders poke it free.
Spinning wildly with no plan — a pivot is a tool, not a tornado.
Forgetting which foot is the pivot after a jump stop — either foot is legal, so pick one and commit.
description: Spin on one foot to protect the ball and create angles — the legal way to turn under pressure.
gameSituations: Catching in the post — pivot to face up or seal the defender.
Trapped on the sideline — reverse pivot away from pressure and pass out.
Rebounding in traffic — pivot away from defenders before the outlet pass.

howTo.detail: When you catch the ball or land (jump stop = either foot; stride stop = back foot), that planted foot is now your pivot foot. It stays glued to the floor.
howTo.title: Establish the pivot foot

howTo.detail: Chin the ball — bring it to your chin with elbows out — and stay in a low athletic stance. The ball is protected before you move.
howTo.title: Protect the ball

howTo.detail: Rotate your body on the ball of the pivot foot, swinging your free foot around. A front pivot turns your chest toward the defender; a reverse pivot turns your back to them.
howTo.title: Rotate on the pivot foot

howTo.detail: Stop the pivot the moment you have an angle — for a pass, a shot, or a drive. Plant the free foot and explode; don't over-rotate.
howTo.title: Pivot into your move

title: Pivoting
whatIsIt: Pivoting is rotating your body on one planted foot — the pivot foot — while the other foot steps freely. It's how you change direction, protect the ball, and create passing or shooting angles without traveling.

Every catch in traffic, every post touch, and every trap situation runs through the pivot. It's the most-used footwork skill in basketball, and also the one that draws the most travels when done sloppily.
whyItMatters: The pivot foot is the line between legal and illegal. Master it and you can operate under pressure — post up, escape traps, face up defenders. Sloppy pivots turn possessions into turnovers. Coaches judge a player's fundamentals largely by how cleanly they pivot.
